name: Sheetswa
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Richards, Erwin H. 1902. Elementary principles of the Sheetswa language. Inhambane: Methodist Episcopal Mission. 35 pp. (public-domain scan, archive.org, Columbia University Libraries)
catalog_locator: section 'Accent', pp. 3-4 (rendered and read); 'partial accent' remark on interrogative 'Ke' p. 15
catalog_quote: Accent. The accent is regularly on the penult. Except (a) when the final vowel is changed to “o” for emphasis, as “Tizoro” for “Tizore”. etc. (b) The enclitic draws the accent forward, as “a ya”, “a ku”. (c) There are a few monosyllabics which retain the accent. As “nzu”, “bi”, “nwa”, etc. Frequently the final vowel is so indistnctly spoken that the word may have the appearance of being accented on the ultima, but the elided vowel always reappears when followed by an enclitic, or some other form of the verb. Example, “Cuwuka”, may be herd as “Cuwuk”. But it is “Cuwukake” or “cuwukela”, when followed as above.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent falls on the penultimate syllable of every word; when an enclitic is attached the accent moves forward so that it stays penultimate in the word+enclitic unit; a few monosyllables keep their own accent; an emphatic final -o attracts the accent; apparent final accent is only the effect of an elided final vowel. Modern descriptions restate the same prominence as non-contrastive penultimate vowel lengthening in a tone language: Kisseberth & Ugembe 2025: 3 'All vowels in Citshwa are basically short vowels.. The penult vowel in the intonational phrase is lengthened'; Gundane 2021: 78 lengthening is 'meramente demarcativo' and 'geralmente ocorre na penúltima sílaba'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source; Richards p. 3/33 notes only that before the interrogative particle 'ke' the preceding syllable and 'ke' each receive 'a partial accent'.
new_statements.exceptions: Richards: emphatic final -o (Tizoro), enclitics shifting the accent, a few accented monosyllables (nzu, bi, nwa); Gundane 2021: lengthening can also fall on the final or initial syllable for emphasis (lènìjá:, khálé:); Gowlett 2003 (Zone S survey): the penultimate length-stress is absent in interrogative and exclamatory sentences.
new_statements.domain_note: Richards states a word-level rule (word + enclitic as the domain). The modern primary sources place the lengthening at phrase level: Kisseberth & Ugembe 2025 'the intonational phrase'; Gowlett 2003 'signals the end of a phrase or sentence'. Citation forms (single words) show penult length in all sources. Tswa is a two-tone (H vs toneless) language; no source calls stress contrastive.
new_statements.identity_note: Richards 1902 describes 'Sheetswa' (= Xitswa) as spoken around the Methodist Episcopal Mission at Inhambane, i.e. coastal Tswa (tswa1255); Kisseberth & Ugembe 2025 and Gundane 2021 describe Citshwa of Inhambane province (Gundane's data from Maxixe, deliberately not restricted to one of the six variants Xikhambani, Xirhonga, Xihlengwe, Ximhandla, Xidzonge, Xidzivi). Gowlett 2003 is a Zone S survey statement that covers Tshwa (S51) but is not language-specific.

sources.citation: Kisseberth, Charles W. & Zeferino Maguiuane Ugembe. 2025. Citshwa phrasal tonology / Tonologia de frase em Citshwa. Revista Científica da Universidade Eduardo Mondlane, Série Letras e Ciências Sociais 5(2): 1-17. DOI 10.70778/vf3hvk84
sources.note: p. 3: 'The tone-bearing unit in Citshwa is the vowel. All vowels in Citshwa are basically short vowels.. The penult vowel in the intonational phrase is lengthened. There is a tonal contrast between whether a vowel has a High tone or not.' Never uses the word stress; examples show penult length (nya:ma, mbú:tí).

sources.citation: Gundane, Lucerio. 2021. Fonologia segmental em Citshwa. Revista Científica da UEM, Série Letras e Ciências Sociais 3(1): 70-89. DOI 10.70778/z6fkwa40
sources.note: p. 75: 'a duração na penúltima sílaba é somente fonética nesta língua'; p. 78: long vowels are 'um alongamento meramente demarcativo que geralmente ocorre na penúltima sílaba, na última ou ainda na primeira sílaba por razões enfáticas.. predizível' (examples mà:mbà, kùkù:mà, lènìjá:, khálé:). No word 'acento'; tonal language, tone marked on all words.

sources.note: §3.6 Accent/stress, p. 617 (survey covering Tshwa S51): 'With the exception of Lozi, Zone S languages have a penultimate length-stress feature which signals the end of a phrase or sentence in declarative sentences. This accent is not used in interrogative and exclamatory sentences.'
